capabilities: Extract entities and relationships from notes with an LLM
Explore and search the knowledge graph interactively
Rank notes and entities by text match and graph proximity
Build editable PubMed and OpenAlex literature searches from graph paths
Serve the vault and graph to AI agents over a local MCP server
disambiguation: Not a graph-visualization enhancement; it builds a separate entity graph from note content using an LLM, alongside its own graph view.
extras: Manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The README warns that provider API keys are stored in data.json and must be added to .gitignore for version-controlled vaults. Local model servers allow fully free, local processing; note analysis with cloud providers costs the provider's per-note pricing.
motivation: The author writes that Obsidian's links between notes make implementing a lightweight ontology model meet users' needs, especially researchers'.
problem: Obsidian links connect notes but does not extract the entities and relationships inside note content into a queryable knowledge graph.

relations.evidence: combines the simplicity of LightRAG with KGGen's hybrid resolution approach
KGGen [3] introduced the insight that entity resolution is critical for quality knowledge graphs
Search follows HippoRAG [6] in ranking by Personalized PageRank over the graph
Bring a med-lit-mcp literature review (articles, wiki pages and its knowledge graph) into your vault
Let Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Codex search your vault and knowledge graph
Develop editable PubMed/OpenAlex searches from explored concepts and paths
Develop editable PubMed/OpenAlex searches from explored concepts and paths

requires.name: LLM provider API key (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek)
MCP agent (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex) for agent access

summary: LLM-powered knowledge graph builder that extracts entities and relationships from notes, with graph exploration, ranked search, and literature search.
